_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); integrated oil and gas signals

pit_profile.why: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business involves exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas and manufacture, trade, transport and sale of crude oil, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemicals and a wide variety of specialty products'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas, and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of alternative energy sources' and 'Due to concern over the risks of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions', which 'could make our products more expensive, less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shift hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas' (its own FY2019 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; re-filed under the energy transition: the theme registry dates its market pricing to ExxonMobil's removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average (S&P Dow Jones Indices, announced 2020-08-24: 'Salesforce.com (NYSE:CRM) will replace Exxon Mobil Corp. (NYSE:XOM)', effective 2020-08-31; the announcement gives as its reason 'prompted by DJIA constituent Apple Inc.'s (NASD:AAPL) decision to split its stock 4:1'), while ExxonMobil's own FY2019 10-K says 'reduce demand for hydrocarbons'

classification.quality_note: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business involves exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas and manufacture, trade, transport and sale of crude oil, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemicals and a wide variety of specialty products'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas, and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of alternative energy sources' and 'Due to concern over the risks of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions', which 'could make our products more expensive, less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shift hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas' (its own FY2019 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; re-filed under the energy transition: the theme registry dates its market pricing to ExxonMobil's removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average (S&P Dow Jones Indices, announced 2020-08-24: 'Salesforce.com (NYSE:CRM) will replace Exxon Mobil Corp. (NYSE:XOM)', effective 2020-08-31; the announcement gives as its reason 'prompted by DJIA constituent Apple Inc.'s (NASD:AAPL) decision to split its stock 4:1'), while ExxonMobil's own FY2019 10-K says 'reduce demand for hydrocarbons'. TRANSITION-exposed franchise (obsolescence risk 3/5); price rich; +60% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.56; conservative 2yr -15%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -53.9%/yr (worst year FY10-FY19, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-29.3%/yr (Q4 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY20 median

BULL.desc: EPS +-10.7%/yr (FY10-FY19 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +61.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY10-FY19); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: XOM (retrospective, 2021-02-12) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (92.1% downside to Bear $4 / +-20.8% upside to Bull $40) | Adj composite 1.27 vs market 2.84: gap -1.56 [OVERVALUED] | +60% above the EPP floor $32 (14x FY21E $2.25) | Conservative 2-yr case: -14.6% total (-7.3%/yr) | At 22.5x FY21E the 15% hurdle price $67 sits above the BULL case; oil-equivalent production -8.2% in Q4 2020, forward revenues -30.7% (no Q1 2021 revenue guide, Q4 2020 revenue as reported); the energy transition is live and re-filed: the theme registry dates its market pricing to ExxonMobil's removal from the Dow Jones Industrial Average (effective 2020-08-31).
